parameters.query:
-- Customers whose attach window on a started room is about to close.
--
-- window_closes_in_days is attach_window_days minus days_since_last_piece,
-- so NEGATIVE means the window already shut and the moment has passed. The
-- 0..7 band is the last week in which a suggestion is still timely.
--
-- consent_email is checked here rather than before the send: a query that
-- cannot return a non-consenting customer is a stronger guarantee than a
-- branch someone can later reorder.
select
  rc.customer_id,
  c.customer_name,
  c.city,
  c.segment,
  rc.room,
  rc.completion_pct,
  rc.anchor_title,
  rc.next_best_title,
  rc.next_best_price,
  rc.next_best_attach_rate,
  rc.room_value_remaining,
  rc.window_closes_in_days
from v_room_completion rc
join v_customer_360 c on c.customer_id = rc.customer_id
where rc.next_best_title is not null
  and rc.window_closes_in_days between 0 and 7
  and c.consent_email = true
  and c.has_email = true
order by rc.room_value_remaining desc
limit 25;

nodes.name: Rooms closing this week
nodes.notes: Uses the read-only agent credential (CADENCE_AGENT_DSN). v_room_completion and v_customer_360 are both inside the five views that role may read.

nodes.name: Attach rate ≥ 25%?
nodes.notes: Suggesting a piece only a quarter of anchor-buyers ever add is a guess. Below the line it goes to a rep instead of an automated send.

nodes.name: Draft message
nodes.notes: Runs once per item — 25 rows in, 25 drafts out.

nodes.name: Send via Resend
nodes.notes: from is 'onboarding@resend.dev' because RESEND_FROM is not set in .env.local and a custom domain must be verified in the Resend account before it can send — see lib/messaging.ts's own fallback. `to` is 'delivered@resend.dev', one of Resend's own reserved test addresses (delivered/bounced/complained/suppressed) — without a verified domain, Resend rejects any other recipient outright, including placeholders like rep@example.com, which two earlier versions of this node both used. v_customer_360 masks PII and exposes has_email, never the address itself, so there is no real address to send to yet either way — point this at a real recipient (and a verified sending domain) only once the send is approved.
